launchers.name: Space Station deployment
launchers.tooltip: Your CubeSat rides up on a cargo flight to the Space Station, then is pushed out into orbit. Cheap, but you get the Station's low orbit.
launchers.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 section 3.5: ISS deployment mission model. Price is a rounded estimate.

launchers.name: CubeSat rideshare
launchers.tooltip: Your CubeSat shares a rocket with a bigger satellite and is released from a dispenser. You go where the main satellite goes.
launchers.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 chapter 3: CubeSats ride as secondary payloads in dispensers. Price is a rounded estimate.

launchers.name: Small rocket
launchers.tooltip: A rocket of your own for small satellites. You choose the orbit and the date, but it costs much more than sharing.
launchers.sourceNote: Generic small launcher class; capacity and price rounded from public figures.

launchers.name: Medium rocket
launchers.tooltip: A workhorse rocket that can lift large satellites to low orbit, and small ones all the way to GEO.
launchers.sourceNote: Generic medium launcher class; capacity and price rounded from public figures.

launchers.name: Heavy rocket
launchers.tooltip: A big rocket for heavy satellites and high orbits like GEO.
launchers.sourceNote: Generic heavy launcher class; capacity and price rounded from public figures.

launchers.name: Super-heavy rocket
launchers.tooltip: The biggest class of rocket. Far more than a satellite usually needs.
launchers.sourceNote: Generic super-heavy launcher class; capacity and price rounded from public figures.
